corpus_title: Masanumasika Garbhini Paricharya Classical Knowledge Base

charaka.sanskrit_shloka: तत्र प्रथमे मासे क्षीरमनुपस्कृतं मात्रावत् काले काले पिबेत्, सात्म्यमेव च सायं प्रातरशनमश्नीयात्।
charaka.regimen: Anupaskrita paya (unprocessed/plain boiled cold milk) in repeated desired quantities; Satmya bhojana (wholesome, habitual light food) morning and evening.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Prevents dehydration and nausea; supplies essential fluids and cooling bio-nutrients during the critical implantation and Kalala phase.

sushruta.regimen: Madhura, Sheeta, and Drava aahara (Sweet, cooling, and unctuous liquid diet).
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Pacifies Pitta and Vata, soothing mucosal lining and preventing early Garbhasrava (spontaneous abortion).

vagbhata.sanskrit_shloka: क्षीरं पयोऽनुपस्कृतं काले काले च पाययेत्। सात्म्यं प्रातश्च सायं च भोजनं मधुरं लघु॥
vagbhata.regimen: Unprocessed milk at frequent intervals; easily digestible light sweet meals morning and evening.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Provides continuous Garbhasthapaka protective effect and keeps gastric mucosa buffered.

kashyapa.regimen: Milk processed with Madhura gana dravyas along with slight Ghrita.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Maintains Dhatu nourishment and stabilizes embryonic sac adhesion.

pathya_do: Luke-warm boiled or cooled plain cow's milk (Godugdha)
Lightly sweet, watery rice gruel (Peya or Vilepi)
Easily digestible fresh fruits like sweet pomegranate (Dadima) or Munakka water
Adequate rest and stress-free environment
apathya_dont: Teekshna (sharp), Ushna (hot potency), and Katu (pungent/spicy) food
Fasting (Upavasa) or skipping meals
Heavy lifting, travel on bumpy roads, and sexual intercourse (Vyavaya)
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 1–4: Blastocyst implantation and embryogenesis. Crucial period for preventing threatened miscarriage; aligns with high hydration, folic acid-rich nourishment, and bland anti-emetic diet.

data.garbha_avastha: Ghana / Peshi / Arbuda (Solidification / Mass formation - Weeks 5 to 8)

charaka.regimen: Milk boiled and medicated with Madhuroushadhas (sweet drugs such as Vidari, Shatavari, Yashtimadhu).
charaka.clinical_rationale: Aids embryonic cell differentiation and alleviates peak hyperemesis gravidarum.

sushruta.regimen: Milk processed with drugs of the Madhura (Kakolyadi) group.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Nourishes the maternal Rasavaha and Raktavaha srotas as maternal blood volume begins to expand.

vagbhata.regimen: Sweet-herb medicated milk with small measure of cow's ghee.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Soothes Pitta aggrevated during embryonic organ-bud development.

kashyapa.regimen: Milk prepared specifically with Shatavari and Vidarikanda.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Potent phytoestrogenic and adaptogenic support for the luteal-placental shift.

pathya_do: Milk infused with Shatavari, Yashtimadhu, or Vidari
Rice cooked with milk (Ksheeranna) in moderate quantity
Frequent small sips of lukewarm water or coconut water for nausea
apathya_dont: Strong smells triggering emesis
Suppression of natural urges (Vega-dharana, especially vomiting and urination)
Fermented, sour, or stale food
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 5–8: Organogenesis stage with peak hCG levels and morning sickness. Medicated milk provides hydration, calories, and gastric mucosal cytoprotection.

data.garbha_avastha: Panchapindika Nirvritti (Initial sprout of 5 bodily extremities and head - Weeks 9 to 12)

charaka.regimen: Milk combined with Madhu (honey) and Ghrita (cow's ghee) in unequal proportions.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Provides instant micro-nutrients and bio-available lipids while balancing Agni.

sushruta.regimen: Milk medicated with sweet herbs taken along with Ghrita.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Promotes embryonic stability and structural formation of limb buds.

vagbhata.sanskrit_shloka: तृतीये सर्पिषा क्षौद्रेण युक्तं पयो हितम्।
vagbhata.regimen: Milk mixed with unequal parts of honey and ghee.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Prevents tissue catabolism and balances Vata-Pitta.

kashyapa.regimen: Ghee and honey enriched milk for firm Garbha stabilization.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Forms essential cellular lipid membranes and strengthens placental bed.

pathya_do: Milk with 1/2 teaspoon Goghrita and 1/4 teaspoon pure Madhu (strictly unequal amounts)
Shashtika Shali (aged red rice) porridge
Sweet, cooling desserts in small portions
apathya_dont: Mixing equal volumes of Honey and Ghee (Samashana viruddha)
Direct exposure to intense heat or sun (Aatapa sevana)
Night vigilance (Ratri jagarana)
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 9–12: Completion of first trimester; placenta takes over endocrine functions. Lipids and glucose polymers fuel rapid fetal growth.

data.garbha_avastha: Vyakti & Dauhrida Avastha (Fetal differentiation & Double-heart desire expression - Weeks 13 to 16)

charaka.regimen: Cow's milk with Navaneeta (fresh unsalted butter) in Aksha-matra (approx. 12g) dose.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Supplies pure unoxidized lipids for myelin sheath synthesis and neurological expansion as fetal organs become prominent.

sushruta.sanskrit_shloka: चतुर्थे षष्टिकान्नं पयसा दध्ना वा भोजयेत्, नवनीतं च दद्यात्।
sushruta.regimen: Shashtika rice served with milk or fresh curd; fresh butter.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Provides sustained carbohydrates and probiotic gut protection for maternal digestion.

vagbhata.regimen: Milk integrated with fresh butter taken regularly.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Assists maternal plasma volume expansion without elevating arterial pressure.

kashyapa.sanskrit_shloka: दौहृदविमाननाद् गर्भस्य विकृतिर्भवति, तस्मात् प्रियं दद्यात्।
kashyapa.regimen: Strict Dauhrida-purana (fulfilling all reasonable maternal maternal culinary desires) along with Navaneeta.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Prevents psychological stress and neuro-developmental fetal deformities.

pathya_do: Fresh unsalted home-churned butter (Navaneeta) with milk
Nutritious grain bowls (rice, barley) with fresh curd/buttermilk
Fulfilment of positive dietary cravings (Dauhrida)
apathya_dont: Repressing maternal cravings (Dauhrida vimanana)
Excessively salty or dry preserved food
Prolonged stationary sitting or standing
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 13–16: Quickening period, maternal circulatory expansion, fetal muscular and skeletal growth. Demand for calcium, fats, and psycho-emotional wellbeing.

data.garbha_avastha: Mamsa-Shonita Upachaya & Mana Chetana (Muscular/blood enrichment & Mind activation - Weeks 17 to 20)

charaka.regimen: Milk medicated or combined directly with cow's ghee (Ghrita).
charaka.clinical_rationale: Nourishes Mamsa and Shonita Dhatus of both mother and fetus, preventing maternal emaciation (Karshya).

sushruta.sanskrit_shloka: पञ्चमे क्षीरसर्पिर्युक्तं षष्टिकान्नं भोजयेत्, जाङ्गलमांसं च।
sushruta.regimen: Shashtika rice with milk and ghee; Jangala mamsa rasa (meat broth of arid-land animals) where indicated.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: High-protein and bioavailable iron input for fetal muscle and red cell production.

vagbhata.sanskrit_shloka: पञ्चमे सर्पिषा युक्तं क्षीरं मांसरसं च वा।
vagbhata.regimen: Milk with ghee or wholesome nutrient-dense soups/broths.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Strengthens maternal stamina and supports fetal somatic muscle accretion.

kashyapa.regimen: Liberal intake of medicated ghee and cow's milk.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Crucial for mental awakening (Chetana) and sensory organ maturation.

pathya_do: Milk mixed with pure Goghrita
Protein-rich broths (Mudga yusha or light Jangala soup for non-vegetarians)
Iron and mineral-rich foods (cooked spinach, dates, soaked raisins)
apathya_dont: Extreme physical workouts or trekking
Dehydrating foods and dry roasted grains without unction
Anger, grief, or violent entertainment
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 17–20: Rapid somatic growth, sensory development, active fetal movements. High maternal iron, protein, and essential fatty acid requirements.

data.garbha_avastha: Buddhi, Varna & Bala Vriddhi (Intellect, complexion & somatic strength - Weeks 21 to 24)

charaka.sanskrit_shloka: षष्ठे मासे पयो घृतसंसृष्टं मधुरौषधसिद्धं पिबेत्।
charaka.regimen: Milk and ghee medicated with drugs belonging to the Madhura gana.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Balances emerging Vata caused by growing intra-abdominal pressure and supports fetal neurological development.

sushruta.regimen: Ghee or Yavagu (gruel) medicated with Shvadamshtra (Gokshura - Tribulus terrestris).
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Acts as a potent Mutrala (mild natural diuretic), relieving gestational pedal edema and water retention.

vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Protects maternal renal clearance while maintaining fetal growth parameters.

kashyapa.regimen: Gokshura Ghrita intake to avert maternal swelling and urinary discomfort.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Maintains fluid homeostasis and microvascular tone.

pathya_do: Gokshura-infused warm water or Gokshura Ghrita (under doctor supervision)
Fluid balance monitoring and elevation of legs when resting
Light, warm meals seasoned with jeera and coriander
apathya_dont: Excessive sodium/salt consumption (Lavana atisevana)
Tight waist garments or restrictive clothing
Sleeping flat on the back for long periods (supine hypotensive syndrome risk)
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 21–24: Increased plasma volume leading to physiological edema; screening window for gestational hypertension. Gokshura provides safe nephro-protective and diuretic balance.

data.garbha_avastha: Sarva Anga Pratyanga Sampoornata & Kikka (All organs fully formed; appearance of striae gravidarum - Weeks 25 to 28)

charaka.sanskrit_shloka: सप्तमे मासे पयो घृतसंसृष्टं मधुरौषधसिद्धं पूर्ववदेव, किक्किसचिकित्सां च कुर्यात्।
charaka.regimen: Sweet-herb medicated milk and ghee; specialized management for Kikkisa (abdominal itching and stretch marks).
charaka.clinical_rationale: Relieves mechanical stretching and itching caused by growing uterus pushing Vidahi Doshas toward the skin.

sushruta.regimen: Yavagu medicated with Vidarigandhadi gana herbs and ghee.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Sustains placental nutrition and strengthens maternal abdominal wall.

vagbhata.regimen: External abhyanga with Karaveera taila, Chandana lepa, or fine herbal pastes; internally medicated ghee.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Soothes cutaneous nerve endings, relieves pruritus and preserves skin elasticity.

kashyapa.regimen: Gentle local application of Navaneeta or Nimba-patra kalka on itchy areas.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Prevents epidermal tearing and secondary excoriation infections.

pathya_do: Frequent small, non-gas-producing meals to ease gastric reflux
Topical application of coconut oil, fresh butter, or Chandana paste on abdomen
Vidarigandhadi or Madhuradravya medicated gruels
apathya_dont: Scratching the abdomen with fingernails (Nakhakshata)
Large heavy single meals (overeating)
Holding back bowel movements (constipation prevention is vital)
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 25–28: Striae gravidarum and pruritus gravidarum appear; fetal lungs start surfactant production; fundal height causes diaphragm and stomach elevation.

data.garbha_avastha: Asthira Ojas (Ojas alternates between mother and fetus - Weeks 29 to 32)

charaka.sanskrit_shloka: अष्टमे मासे क्षीरयवागूं सर्पिष्मतीमश्नीयात्, आस्थापनं च दद्यात् स्निग्धं बस्तिकर्म।
charaka.regimen: Ksheera Yavagu (rice gruel cooked in milk) with abundant ghee; unctuous Asthapana and Anuvasana Basti protocol.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Because Ojas is unstable (Asthira), high-calorie, easily assimilable Ksheera Yavagu is required; gentle Basti calms Apana Vayu to avert preterm labor.

sushruta.sanskrit_shloka: अष्टमे बद्धविट्काया निरूहमास्थापयेत्, पयसा यवागूं च दद्यात्।
sushruta.regimen: Asthapana basti for relieving severe constipation, followed by milk gruel with ghee.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Relieves severe lower pelvic congestion and rectal distension without triggering hyper-peristalsis.

vagbhata.regimen: Milk gruel enriched with ghee and regulated gentle cleansing basti.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Safeguards against premature delivery in the fragile Ojas-transition phase.

kashyapa.sanskrit_shloka: ओजश्चञ्चलतैव स्यादष्टमे मासि सर्वदा, तस्माद् यत्नेन रक्षेत्।
kashyapa.regimen: Continuous monitoring and nourishing, unctuous regimen to shield maternal energy.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: If delivery occurs in this month, survival is endangered due to incomplete Ojas stabilization.

pathya_do: Warm milk gruel (Ksheera Yavagu) with pure cow's ghee
High dietary fiber and adequate warm fluids to prevent hard stools
Gentle rest and minimal travel
apathya_dont: Rough, dry, constipating foods (Ruksha ahara)
Any harsh purgation (Teekshna Virechana is contraindicated)
Intercity or bumpy vehicular travel
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 29–32: Preterm birth during this window carries high risk due to pulmonary and immune immaturity (correlating to classical Asthira Ojas). Basti alleviates pelvic venous stasis.

data.garbha_avastha: Sampoornata & Prasava Sannidhi (Term maturity & preparation for normal parturition - Weeks 33 to 40)

charaka.sanskrit_shloka: नवमे मासे मधुरौषधसिद्धेन तैलेनानुवासनबस्तिं दद्यात्, तैलपिचुं च योनौ प्रणयेत्।
charaka.regimen: Anuvasana Basti with oil medicated with Madhura gana drugs (e.g., Bala Taila); daily retention of oil swab (Taila Pichu) in the vaginal canal.
charaka.clinical_rationale: Softens the birth canal, relaxes pelvic ligaments, lubricates perineal tissues, and normalizes Apana Vayu for frictionless natural labor (Sukha Prasava).

sushruta.regimen: Unctuous gruels, local pelvic oleation, and vaginal lubrication with Taila Pichu.
sushruta.clinical_rationale: Facilitates downward movement of the fetus and ensures flexibility of the soft birth passage.

vagbhata.sanskrit_shloka: मधुरौषधतैलेन बस्तिं दद्यात् पिशुं तथा। सुखप्रसवसिद्ध्यर्थं मारुतस्यानुलोमनात्॥
vagbhata.regimen: Anuvasana basti and vaginal tampon (Pichu) using Bala Taila.
vagbhata.clinical_rationale: Vata Anulomana ensures physiological coordinated uterine contractions and prevents obstructed labor (Mudha Garbha).

kashyapa.regimen: Preparation of Sutikagara (birthing suite/maternity ward) and routine Bala Taila Pichu.
kashyapa.clinical_rationale: Prepares maternal physical and mental readiness for safe delivery.

pathya_do: Daily or regular Bala Taila Pichu (sterile medicated cotton tampon in vagina, as advised by gynecologist/Ayurvedic doctor)
Warm, easily digestible unctuous foods (Ghee with warm soups)
Gentle walking and pelvic floor breathing exercises
apathya_dont: Suppressing urge to pass urine or stools
Cold baths or cold dry food items
Mental panic, fear, or anxiety about labor pain
practical_guidelines.modern_correlation: Weeks 33–40: Cervical ripening, pelvic floor relaxation, and fetal descent. Taila Pichu acts as a perineal emollient and cervical preparation mechanism, supporting safe vaginal delivery.
